outcomes: A team that keeps its decisions as MADR files sees, for each change, the decisions that govern the files it touches, with their status, in the detailed summary and in the change evidence document
A change that adds, edits or deletes a decision record lists it, and a change that deletes an accepted decision is flagged
Nothing is converted and no decision is required: a repository without decision records observes as before
nonGoals: Writing, converting or validating decision records, or requiring a scope
Judging whether a change complies with a decision: the document reports which decisions govern the change, not a verdict
Decision formats other than MADR Markdown files, and the decisions.json of a Putnami workspace

text: Decision records are the .md files under the directories --decisions names, comma-separated and relative to the repository root, else docs/decisions and docs/adr, walked recursively past hidden directories.
An entry outside the repository is a diagnostic and is not read.
README.md, index.md and a file whose name holds template are not records, and a directory that does not exist is no diagnostic.
A record's title is its front matter title, else its first level-one heading, else its file name.
Its status is the front matter status, else the value of a Status line, plain, in a list item or in bold, else the first line of a Status section;
the first word, lowercased, gives proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated or superseded, and anything else unknown.
Its date is the front matter date, else the value of a Date line, kept when it is a valid YYYY-MM-DD date.

A record's scope is its front matter scope, a list or one pattern, else the list items of its Scope section, each one path pattern, with its backticks removed when it is quoted in them, else up to its first space.
No scope is valid: the record then governs nothing.
A scope pattern is relative to the repository root; a leading ./ or / and a trailing / are dropped, and a pattern with a drive letter or a .. segment matches nothing.
A pattern without * or ? governs the path itself and every path under it.
Otherwise * and ? match within one segment, a ** segment matches any number of segments, and every other character, [ included, matches itself.

The observation and the evidence document list, sorted by path, every record whose scope matches a changed file, with the changed files it governs, and every record the change adds, modifies, renames or deletes, a record moved out of the decision directories included, with that file status;
records are read at the head and a deleted one at the base.
A record that cannot be read is a diagnostic.
A repository without decision records gets no decisions and no diagnostic.
A change that deletes an accepted decision record gets the warning observe.decision_deleted naming the record.
A superseded or deprecated decision is listed with that status, like any other.

requirements.text: The detailed text summary, which --details prints, lists the decisions under a decisions heading, one line each with its status, its path and its title, then how many changed files it governs and whether the change added, modified, renamed or deleted it.

On a repository with three MADR files, one governing a path by its front matter scope, one by a Scope section and one accepted decision the change deletes, a change under the governed paths lists their decisions in the detailed summary and in the evidence document, which validates, and the deleted accepted decision is flagged.
